Chapter 8. The Cross and the Mystery of Suffering.
Suffering—it's something that touches every single one of us, often in ways we can't quite put into words. You know, the really tough questions come up in these moments: Why do good people go through such pain? Where is God when life just hurts too much to bear?
Instead of glossing over these questions or offering easy fixes, this chapter invites us to sit with the mystery. It’s about letting the cross change the way we see suffering itself.
Picture someone who's just lost a loved one, or maybe they've gotten news from the doctor that changes everything. The first instinct is usually to search for reasons—to try and make sense of the pain. But here’s the thing: the cross doesn’t try to explain suffering away. Instead, it shows us a God who steps right into the mess, a God who knows what it’s like to feel abandoned, misunderstood, even broken.
That really changes the conversation, doesn’t it? Suddenly, suffering isn’t just something to run from. It becomes a place where God actually meets us.
The stories in this chapter are full of people who, right in the middle of their pain, found a strange sense of comfort in the story of the cross. Not because their suffering was made smaller—but because it was shared. The cross is God’s way of saying, “I’m not distant. I’m right here with you, even in the darkness, carrying the weight with you.”
Does that make suffering easy? Of course not. But it does make it bearable. It means pain isn’t a sign that we’ve failed or that we’re being punished. It’s just part of being human.
The cross gives us permission to grieve, to ask hard questions, to cry out when things hurt. It reassures us that every tear is seen—and that not a single bit of our pain is wasted.
